questions.question: Two spheres of masses m and M are situated in air and the gravitational force between them is F. The space between the masses is now filled with a liquid of specific gravity 3. The gravitational force will now be
questions.solution:
__CONCEPT__:

Newton's law of Gravitation:

__
 
• Newton's law of gravitation states that everybody in this universe attracts every other body with a force, which is directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centers.
 
• The direction of the force is along the line joining the particles.
 
• The magnitude of the gravitational force F is

F = G({{M₁)/(M₂)}}{{{R²}}}

Where G = universal gravitational constant, M1 = mass of 1st body, M2 = mass of 2nd body, and R = distance between the two bodies.

EXPLANATION__:

 
• From above it is clear that the gravitational force **depends **on the **mass of the bodies** and the **distance between them**.** **
 
• It is independent of the nature and size of the bodies as well as the nature of the medium between the bodies. Therefore it will remain the same i.e. **F**.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of universal gravitational constant G?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**N m² / kg²**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The universal gravitational constant (**G**) is a fundamental physical constant that appears in Newton's law of universal gravitation.
 
• Its value is approximately **6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² / kg²**.
 
• The SI unit of **G** is derived from the formula of gravitational force: **F = G (m₁m₂) / r²**, where:
 
 
• **F** is the force measured in newtons (N).
 
• **m₁** and **m₂** are masses measured in kilograms (kg).
 
• **r** is the distance between the two masses measured in meters (m).
 
 
 
• From the formula, the unit of **G** is derived as **N m² / kg²**.
 
• **G** is a crucial constant for calculating the gravitational attraction between two objects.
 
• This constant is used in various fields, including **astrophysics, geophysics**, and **space exploration**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **N m² / kg⁻¹**__

 __
 
• This unit is incorrect as the exponent of **kg** should be **-2** instead of **-1**.
 
• The term does not align with Newton's law of universal gravitation and is mathematically incorrect.
 
 
 
• **N kg m²**__
 __
 
• This unit is incorrect because **G** measures a force-related constant, and the unit does not account for the gravitational relationship between masses.
 
• The term does not include the inverse square relationship of distance.
 
 
 
• **N m² / kg s⁻¹**__
 
 
• This unit is incorrect as it includes **seconds (s)**, which is irrelevant to the concept of gravitational force.
 
• **G** does not involve time in its calculations, hence this unit is invalid.

questions.question: While standing on Earth, suppose your weight has a value of 100 Newtons. If the Earth shrinks to half its diameter without any change in mass, then your new weight on the surface of the shrunken Earth, in Newtons, is
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**400.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• Weight of the body (W1) = mg;
 
• The surface of the earth with radius R. (Given 100 Newtons)
 
• Acceleration due to gravity on earth (g) = G.M/R²,
 
 
• G is gravitation constant, (M) is mass of earth and R is the initial radius of the earth.
 
 
 
• Now Final radius =R/2;
 
• New acceleration due to gravity on earth (g2) = (G.M)/(R/2)² = 4(G.M/R²) = 4g
 
• So new weight of Body (W2) = m. g2 = 4(m.g) [as mass of body is constant]
 
• **From above,**
 
 
• **W2 = 4* W1 =4*100 = 400 Newtons**. **Hence option 2 is correct.**

questions.question: If the distance between the earth and the sun were twice what it is now, the gravitational force exerted on the earth by the sun would be:

options.text: four times as large as it is now
half of what it is now
one-fourth of what it is now

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**one-fourth of what it is now.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Surface gravity** varies** inversely with the square of the planet's radius.**
 
• So doubling the radius would reduce gravity by a **factor of four.**
 
• Hence the **gravitational force exerted on the earth by the sun would be one-fourth of what it is now.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

• The gravitational force is a force that attracts any two objects with mass. 
 
• The force of attraction between any two bodies is directly **proportional to the product of their masses** and is **inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.**
 
• **Gravitational force Formula:**
 
• **F = {G.m1.m2over r²}**

questions.question: The acceleration due to gravity on an object of mass m placed near the surface of the earth is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**independent of m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The acceleration due to gravity (g) near the surface of the Earth is approximately 9.81 m/s² and is considered a constant.
 
• It is determined by the Earth's mass and radius, and not by the mass of the object experiencing the acceleration.
 
• The formula for gravitational force is F = G(m1*m2)/r², where G is the gravitational constant, m1 and m2 are the masses, and r is the distance between their centers.
 
• When calculating acceleration due to gravity (g), the mass of the object (m) cancels out, showing that g is independent of m.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gravitational Constant (G)**

 
 
• The gravitational constant (G) is a fundamental physical constant denoted by G.
 
• Its value is approximately 6.674 × 10^-11 N(m/kg)².
 
• This constant is crucial in the calculation of gravitational forces in Newton's law of universal gravitation.
 
 
 
• **Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation**
 
 
• Proposed by Sir Isaac Newton in 1687, it states that every mass attracts every other mass with a force directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centers.
 
• The formula is F = G(m1*m2)/r².
 
 
 
• **Earth's Radius and Mass**
 
 
• The average radius of the Earth is about 6,371 kilometers.
 
• The mass of the Earth is approximately 5.972 × 10^24 kilograms.
 
 
 
• **Free Fall**
 
 
• In free fall, the only force acting on an object is gravity.
 
• All objects in free fall near the Earth's surface accelerate at the same rate, regardless of their mass.

questions.question: What is the weight of an object of mass 40 kg, if the acceleration due to gravity at that place is 9.8 m/s²?
questions.solution:
The correct option is __**392 N.**__

__Concept:__

Acceleration due to gravity:

 
• The acceleration achieved by any object due to the gravitational force of attraction by any planet is called acceleration due to gravity by the earth.
 
• As each planet has a different mass and radius so the acceleration due to gravity will be different for a different planet.

Weight: 

 
• The weight(w) of an object is the force of gravity on the object and may be defined as the mass (m) times the acceleration of gravity (g).
 
• Weight is a force, and the SI unit of weight is Newton.
 
• Weight (F) = m x g

​Moon vs Earth:

 
• The mass of the moon is 1/100 times and the radius of the moon is 1/4 times that of the Earth.
 
• Since the acceleration due to the gravity of the moon is one-sixth of that of the Earth.
 
• So the weight of any object on the Moon = 1/6 × Weight of any object on the Earth's surface.

Calculation:

Given:

m = 40 kg g = 9.8 m/s²

Weight = m x g = 40 × 9.8 = **392 N.**

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?

Statements:

I) The mass of an object is the same as its weight.

II) The mass of an object is not the same as its weight.

III) Mass is scalar quantity, whereas weight is vector quantity.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mass and weight are different physical quantities; mass is a measure of the amount of matter in an object, while weight is the force exerted by gravity on that object.
 
• Mass is a scalar quantity, which means it has magnitude but no direction.
 
• Weight is a vector quantity, as it has both magnitude and direction (towards the center of the Earth).
 
• Statement I is incorrect because mass and weight are not the same.
 
• Statement II is correct as it states the differentiation between mass and weight.
 
• Statement III is correct, further differentiating mass and weight in terms of scalar and vector quantities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mass**

 
 
• It is measured in kilograms (kg) in the International System of Units (SI).
 
• Mass remains constant regardless of location.
 
 
 
• **Weight**
 
 
• It is measured in newtons (N) in the SI system.
 
• Weight varies depending on the gravitational pull of the location (e.g., Earth, Moon).
 
 
 
• **Gravitational Force**
 
 
• It is the force of attraction between two masses.
 
• Gravitational force is responsible for giving objects weight.

options.text: The weight of a given object is 6 times higher on the moon as compared to its weight on the earth.
The weight of a given object is the same when we measure it on the earth or moon.

questions.solution:

__
 
• The weight of an object is a measure of the gravitational force acting on it.
 
• On the moon, gravity is about 1/6th as strong as on Earth.
 
• Therefore, an object will weigh less on the moon compared to its weight on Earth.
 
• The correct statement is that the weight of a given object is 6 times higher on the Earth as compared to its weight on the moon.

• Weight depends on the gravitational force and can change with location.
 
 
 
• **Gravitational Acceleration**
 
 
• On Earth, it is approximately 9.81 m/s².

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are true for the gravitational force between two bodies:

(i) It is repulsive in nature.

(ii) It's magnitude is same throughout the universe.

(iii) It is directly proportional to the product of the masses of the bodies.

(iv) Due to this force the earth goes around the sun.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both (iii) and (iv)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The gravitational force is always **attractive** and never repulsive.
 
• The magnitude of the gravitational force varies based on the **distance** between the two bodies and their masses, not constant throughout the universe.
 
• Gravitational force is **directly proportional** to the product of the masses of the two bodies involved.
 
• This force is responsible for the **earth's orbit around the sun**.
 
• Gravitational force is essential for maintaining the **orbital paths** of planets and other celestial bodies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation:** States that every mass exerts an attractive force on every other mass. The force is proportional to the product of the masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.
 
• **Gravitational Constant (G):** The proportionality constant in Newton's law of gravitation, approximately equal to 6.674 × 10−¹¹ N(m/kg)².
 
• **Mass and Weight:** Mass is the amount of matter in an object, while weight is the force exerted by gravity on that mass.
 
• **Orbital Mechanics:** The study of the motions of artificial satellites and natural celestial bodies under the influence of gravitational forces.
 
• **Einstein's Theory of General Relativity:** Provides a more comprehensive description of gravity, describing it as the curvature of spacetime caused by mass and energy.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true about the free fall of an object under gravitational force?

options.text: The acceleration experienced by an object depends on its mass.
The velocity of the object remains constant during free fall.
The acceleration experienced by an object is independent of its mass.
The acceleration experienced by an object is opposite to the direction of motion.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The acceleration experienced by an object is independent of its mass**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The acceleration due to gravity is denoted by the symbol **g** and has a value of approximately **9.8 m/s²** near the surface of the Earth.
 
• According to the principle of **Galileo's law of falling bodies**, all objects fall at the same rate regardless of their mass when only the gravitational force is acting upon them.
 
• This means that in a vacuum, where there is no air resistance, a feather and a hammer will fall at the same rate.
 
• The concept is also supported by **Newton's second law of motion**, which states that force equals mass times acceleration (F = ma). When considering only gravitational force, the mass of the object cancels out, leaving the acceleration due to gravity constant.
 
• This fundamental principle of physics demonstrates that **acceleration due to gravity** is a constant and does not depend on the mass of the object.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Acceleration experienced by an object depends on its mass**__

 __
 
• This statement is incorrect because the acceleration due to gravity is a constant and does not vary with the mass of the object.
 
 
 
• **The velocity of the object remains constant during free fall**__
 __
 
• This statement is incorrect because the velocity of an object in free fall continues to increase as it falls due to the constant acceleration of gravity.
 
 
 
• **The acceleration experienced by an object is opposite to the direction of motion**__
 
 
• This statement is incorrect because the acceleration due to gravity acts in the direction of motion (downward) when an object is in free fall.

questions.question: A 2-kg object falls from a height of 20 m to the ground. The work done by the force of gravity will be _____. (Take g = 10 m/s2)
questions.solution:
__Concept:__

__
 
• Work is done: The product of force and displacement is called work done
 
• Work was done against gravity: When an object is brought to some height going against gravity, work is said to be done against gravity.
 
 
• This work done is converted into potential energy.
 
• The potential energy is energy stored in a body when work is done against gravity. It is given as 
 
 

P = m × g × h

 
• As for lifting or after lifting at height some work needs to be done, .for e.g A coolie lifting a weight in his weight, it is in the form of potential energy, so work done can also be written as,

W = P = m × g × h.

m is mass, g is the acceleration due to gravity, and h is the height obtained. 

Calculations__:

__
 
• The mass of the object (m) is 2 kg.
 
• The height of the object (h) is 20m
 
• The gravity of the earth (g) is 10 m/s2
 
• Now Work done by the force of gravity = mgh
 
• Now substituting the above values, we get

= 2 x 20 x 10 

= 400 J

 
• The work done by the force of gravity will be 400 J.__

questions.question:
Consider the following phenomena:

1. Light is affected by gravity.

2. The Universe is constantly expanding.

3. Matter warps its surrounding space-time.

Which of the above is/are the prediction/predictions of Albert Einstein's General Theory of Relativity, often discussed in media?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1, 2, and 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The bending of light by gravity can lead to the phenomenon of **gravitational lensing**, in which multiple images of the same distant astronomical object are visible in the sky.
 
• Albert Einstein predicted the existence of gravitational waves in 1916 in his general theory of relativity.
 
• Gravity, Einstein asserted, is caused by a **warping of space and time**. Gravity is the curvature of spacetime caused by massive objects.
 
• In 1917, Einstein applied the general theory of relativity to the structure of the universe as a whole. He found that the general field equations predicted a universe that was dynamic, either contracting or expanding. Since observational evidence for a dynamic universe was not known at the time, Einstein introduced a new term, the cosmological constant, for the field equations to allow him to predict a static universe. In these years the modified field equations predicted a stable universe of closed curvature according to Einstein's understanding of Mach's principle. This model is known as Einstein's world or Einstein's stable universe.

questions.question:
The following statement applies to which law from the given options? 

'The line that joins any planet to the sun sweeps equal areas in equal intervals of time.'
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Law of Areas**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the law of areas, the line joins any planet to the sun sweeps equal areas in equal intervals of time.
 
• When the planet is **closer to the Sun** (at perihelion), it moves **faster**, sweeping out a narrow but long area.
 
• When the planet is **farther from the Sun** (at aphelion), it moves **slower**, sweeping out a wide but shorter area.
 
• This ensures the areas are equal in equal times.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b71c5134ac1d490aef6d0f3851833577d46b39fc9b931d230bb62bf209418a93.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Law of Orbits**

 
 
• **​**The **Law of Orbits** is the **first law** of **Kepler's Laws of Planetary Motion**, which describes the shape of the path a planet takes as it orbits the Sun.
 
• Planets do not move in perfect circles but rather in elliptical (oval-shaped) paths.
 
• An ellipse has two fixed points called **foci**.
 
• The Sun is located at one of these foci, not at the center of the ellipse.
 
 
 
• **Law of Periods **
 
 
• **​**The **Law of Periods** is the **third law** of **Kepler's Laws of Planetary Motion**, describing the relationship between the orbital period of a planet and the size of its orbit.
 
• **Planets farther from the Sun have longer orbital periods** because they travel greater distances and move more slowly due to weaker gravitational forces.
 
• This law applies not only to planets but also to moons, satellites, and other celestial objects orbiting a massive body.
 
 
 
• **Law of Motion **
 
 
• **​**The **Laws of Motion** were formulated by Sir **Isaac Newton** and are fundamental principles in classical mechanics.
 
• These laws describe the relationship between the motion of an object and the forces acting on it.

questions.question: The value of Universal Gravitational constant is G on a certain planet of mass M, on another planet of mass 4M, the value of the Universal Gravitational constant will be:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**G**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Universal Gravitational Constant (G) is a physical constant that is invariant and has the same value in all locations in the universe.
 
• Its value is approximately 6.67430 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg².
 
• The value of G does not depend on the masses or the distance between the objects; it remains constant.
 
• The gravitational force between two masses is given by Newton's law of universal gravitation, which incorporates the constant G.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation:**

 
 
• It states that every point mass attracts every other point mass in the universe with a force that is directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centers.
 
 
 
• **Formula for Gravitational Force (F):**
 
 
• F = (Gm₁m₂)/(r²)
 
• Where F is the gravitational force, G is the gravitational constant, m₁ and m₂ are the masses of the objects, and r is the distance between the centers of the two masses.
 
 
 
• **Importance of G:**
 
 
• G is crucial for calculating gravitational forces in physics, astronomy, and engineering.
 
• It helps in understanding the motion of planets, stars, and galaxies.
 
 
 
• **Variation of Gravitational Force:**
 
 
• While G remains constant, the gravitational force can vary based on the masses involved and the distance between them.
 
• This variation is described by the inverse-square law.

questions.question: The motion of the moon around the earth is due to the:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Centripetal force**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **motion of the moon** around the Earth is governed by the **centripetal force**.
 
• **Centripetal force** is a force that acts toward the **center of a circular path**, keeping an object in circular motion.
 
• In the case of the moon, this force is provided by the **gravitational pull of the Earth**.
 
• The **gravitational force** acts as the centripetal force, pulling the moon toward the Earth and preventing it from moving off in a straight line due to its inertia.
 
• Without this force, the moon would follow a straight-line path into space, as per **Newton's first law of motion**.
 
• The balance between the moon's tangential velocity and the centripetal force keeps it in a stable **orbital motion** around the Earth.
 
• This principle applies to all celestial bodies in orbit, including **planets, satellites, and stars** in their respective systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Centrifugal force**__

 __
 
• **Centrifugal force** is a fictitious force that appears to act outward on a body in a rotating reference frame.
 
• It is not a real force but rather the result of inertia when viewed in a non-inertial, rotating frame.
 
• In contrast to the **centripetal force**, it does not play a role in the moon's motion, as the moon orbits due to the Earth's gravitational pull.
 
 
 
• **Coriolis force**__
 __
 
• The **Coriolis force** is an apparent force caused by the rotation of the Earth.
 
• It primarily affects the motion of objects over large distances, such as **air currents and ocean currents**, causing them to deflect to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere.
 
• It is not responsible for the orbital motion of celestial bodies.
 
 
 
• **Coulomb force**__
 
 
• The **Coulomb force** refers to the electrostatic force between two charged particles.
 
• It has no role in the motion of the moon, as the moon and the Earth interact primarily through **gravitational force**, not electrostatic force.

questions.question: Calculate the gravitational potential energy of a 50 kg object placed 5 meters above the ground. (Use g = 9.8 m/s²​)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **2450** J

**Calculation:**

m = 50 kg

h = 5m,

g = 9.8 m/s²

Using the formula for gravitational potential energy:

U = mgh

U = 50 × 9.8 × 5

U = 2450 J

**So, gravitational potential energy is 2450 J**
